name: L'Rain
label: Mexican Summer
lede: A Brooklyn curator with a basement venue, a pink Cadillac radio station and a stage name from her mother, who by 2026 has an 8.2 from Pitchfork for a record about not being boxed in.

eras.title: Ailey, Yale, and a band called Throw Vision
eras.text: Crown Heights kid, ballet and modern dance at the Ailey School, piano, cello and Baroque recorder before bass. Yale by way of American Studies, then a Brooklyn band and a day job in the art world.

years.h: Yale radio music director, American Studies degree
years.p: Taja Cheek graduates with distinction after starting as a music major and running the music desk at campus station WYBC.
years.xp:
Cheek had studied ballet and modern dance at the Ailey School as a kid, and picked up piano, cello and Baroque recorder before taking up bass in high school. At Yale she moved from music to American Studies, with a concentration built around visual, audio, literary and performance cultures.

Wikipedia lists her parents as Wyatt Cheek, a music marketing professional, and Lorraine C. Porter, an educator. Lorraine is where the stage name comes from.

years.src: Bedford + Bowery: Throw Vision · Wikipedia: L'Rain
years.h: Throw Vision starts as a trio in Brooklyn
years.p: Cheek plays keys in a band that mixes jazz harmony, rock and ambient drift, later adding a fourth member.
years.xp:
Bedford + Bowery described a four-piece of Taja, Tiff, Alex and Dan in 2015: Cheek with classical piano and a jazz ear, one member trained in ethnomusicology, a classical percussionist new to rock bands, and a blues and improv guitarist. The trio formed in 2012, the fourth member came later.

Their limited clear-vinyl 7-inch, Were It Will, came out of songs worked up live, and the band played Palisades, the Knitting Factory and C'mon Everybody in Bed-Stuy that summer. Wikipedia dates a debut to 2013 and an EP to 2015.

eras.title: Radio from a pink Cadillac
eras.text: Cheek spends her twenties on the other side of the stage: producing art in public for Creative Time, then programming outdoor shows at MoMA PS1, while starting a basement venue of her own.

years.cap: The pop-up radio station in Bed-Stuy, 2014.
years.src: Wikipedia: L'Rain · Ben Sisto: JOB Interview
years.h: A pop-up radio station in a pink Cadillac on Utica Avenue
years.p: As site manager of a Creative Time and Weeksville Heritage Center project, Cheek runs a working radio station out of a pink Cadillac parked at the A/C stop.
years.xp:
Cheek was a Creative Time fellow before moving into curating, and told Ben Sisto the job taught her grant writing and how the contemporary art world works. The same year she co-organized the Kara Walker project at the Domino Sugar Refinery with Ariana Allensworth, Salome Asega, Sable Elyse Smith and Nadia Williams.

Two years later she was at MoMA PS1, running the Sunday Sessions and Warm Up courtyard series. She kept the curator and musician sides deliberately apart in that period, she told Sisto.

years.src: Wikipedia: L'Rain · Ben Sisto: JOB Interview
years.h: 49 Shade: shows in her basement apartment
years.p: Cheek opens the basement under her Brooklyn apartment to experimental music, listed on Oh My Rockness, with co-organizers Max Alper, Dann Lawrence and Matteo Liberatore.
years.xp: Kyp Malone, Miho Hatori and Otomo Yoshihide have all played 49 Shade. Bartees Strange has credited the room with connecting him to collaborators, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: A stage name that was her mother's idea
eras.text: The first L'Rain record arrives on a small Brooklyn label, credited to a project named for Lorraine Porter, who died while it was being made.

years.p: Cheek plays nearly everything, samples hundreds of field recordings and gets backing vocals from Kyp Malone of TV on the Radio.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Andrew Lappin on guitars and as co-producer, Alex Goldberg on drums and Jeremy Powell on saxophone. Pitchfork's Jay Balfour gave it 6.8, calling it a beautiful, untidy conduit for Cheek's emotional processing, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork put it on its list of 20 best experimental albums of 2017 and Bandcamp Daily ranked it #10 overall.

years.cap: The debut's cover shows a tattoo of the name on Cheek's forearm.
q: I realized after the first album was released that L'Rain was my mom's idea all along.
years.src: BOMB Magazine: Taja Cheek · Wikipedia: L'Rain (album)
years.p: Cheek's mother, Lorraine, died while the debut was being made. The name is hers.
years.xp:
The album cover is a photograph of the name tattooed on Cheek's forearm. In a 2021 BOMB interview, Cheek said she realized after the first album that L'Rain was her mom's idea all along.

Her mother had encouraged her to sing and play piano on her own, and Lappin, a friend, asked for a solo record after her band projects had dissolved.

years.h: A 1980s Chicago house track for a prison-abolition benefit
years.p: Cheek, Morgan Wiley and Patrick Gordon remake "Your Love" for the Bring Down the Walls compilation, which raised money for Critical Resistance.
years.xp: The remake shows the other L'Rain: a dance floor reader who is as comfortable with a house classic as with a field recording.

eras.title: Twenty players and one very long sigh
eras.text: Fatigue lands on Mexican Summer with a cast of twenty and the critics' attention, and Cheek starts opening for bigger, weirder bands.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fatigue (album) · BOMB Magazine: Taja Cheek
years.p: Recorded in Brooklyn and at Sunset Sound in Los Angeles, the record samples a pastor singing at a funeral Cheek attended on "Find It".
years.xp:
She almost called it Suck Teeth, because she loved how it captured a very black sound of disapproval, annoyance and disappointment, according to Wikipedia. The phrase became a song instead. "Black Clap" uses sounds from a hand game she made with co-producer Ben Chapoteau-Katz.

Pitchfork gave it 8.5, per Wikipedia. The Wire named it album of the year, and Metacritic sits at 86/100. AllMusic called it bolder and dreamier than the debut.

years.src: BOMB Magazine: Taja Cheek · Wikipedia: L'Rain
years.h: Touring with black midi, sitting the crowd down first
years.p: Cheek plays support dates for black midi and asks audiences to sit before her set, a habit she described to BOMB.
years.xp: She told BOMB she often plays bars and dingy clubs and likes creating a bit of dissonance to transform them into somewhere else, using vocal loops, smudging and softness. Cheek's band at the time included Chapoteau-Katz, guitarist and bassist Justin Felton and drummer Alwyn Robinson.

years.h: Opening for Animal Collective and Sharon Van Etten
years.p: Cheek takes her looped, layered live show on the road with two bigger names, and is listed as a former MoMA PS1 associate curator by July.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists her as a former associate curator at MoMA PS1 by July 2022.

eras.title: Bratty, diabolical, dad rock
eras.text: I Killed Your Dog is the loudest joke she has made, and the tour dates get much bigger.

years.h: I Killed Your Dog · a bratty "anti-break-up" record
years.p: Cheek calls it a bolder, brattier, more diabolical side of L'Rain, mixing indie dad rock with experimental electronics.
years.xp:
It was recorded across seven studios, including Abbey Road in London, Gary's Electric in Brooklyn and Wax Ltd in Hollywood. Singles were "New Year's UnResolution", "Pet Rock" (the video uses miniatures) and "r (Emote)".

Metacritic gave it 87/100, and Pitchfork named it Best New Music and ranked it 12th on its 2023 year-end list, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Celebrate Brooklyn! names her its first artist curator
years.p: BRIC's summer festival hands Cheek the lineup, the same job she did for years at MoMA PS1.

years.h: Tour dates with Big Thief and LCD Soundsystem
years.p: Cheek opens for Big Thief and LCD Soundsystem in the year I Killed Your Dog comes out, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Yes/and
eras.text: fata morgana is billed as the fourth and last part of a run that began in 2017, and the first that treats the experimental label as a limit.

years.big: Is this a glass ceiling or not?
q: I was just noticing how people were treating my music with white gloves.
years.src: NPR: L'Rain's 'fata morgana' rewrites pop in her own image · Spectrum Culture: L'Rain: fata morgana
years.h: Cheek asks whether the ceiling above her music is glass
years.p: Before fata morgana, Cheek told the New York Times how people around her handled her music: with white gloves.
years.xp: As NPR reads the album, she is asking whether the barriers between her and mainstream pop are structural or self-imposed. NPR calls it both alien and familiar, "yes/and" and not "either/or".

years.src: The Fork: L'Rain fata morgana · Wikipedia: Fata Morgana (L'Rain album) · Paste: Review: L'Rain is in full control · Spectrum Culture: L'Rain: fata morgana
years.p: Stephen Kearse's Pitchfork review scores Cheek's fourth album 8.2. The lead single is "soulless cycle" (June 10), followed by "borderline" (July 8).
years.xp:
Cheek describes it as the last part of a continuum, the fourth record of a quadrilogy that revisits her mother's death, romantic ambiguity, exhaustion and looking for meaning in America now. It was made at Gary's Electric in Brooklyn with Ben Chapoteau-Katz and Andrew Lappin, and Welterweight Sound in Marlboro, NY, with sequencing by Yuka Honda.

The 13 tracks run about 39 minutes and take in dancehall, tape meditation, slow jams, gospel and crunched metal. Screechy Dan sings a dancehall outro on "july 5th". Paste gave it an A-, and Metacritic sits at 86/100. Lappin called the sound "craggy", per Spectrum Culture.
